title: The reduced form at every order: the Jordan chains of the cut-open torus at powers of two
claim: At n = 2^m, h = n/2, q = 2n, for a in GF(q)* with b = sqrt(a), Z(w) = S + M_(Omega(w)) the family of JORDAN-CHAINS-20261110-001A, G the monic least-degree element of ker X_b, k = h - deg G, J = ceil(k/2), N = G(k) G(k + 1), u = (w - a)/a and L(x) = x + x^2 + x^4 + ...: (1) Omega(a + d) = (1 + d/a)(Omega_a + sum over r = 1..m-1 of d^(2^r) k^(h - 2^(r-1))) mod d^n, so near a, Z(w) = S + (w/a)(b + k^h L(w^2/k)); (2) near every a, Z(w) is equivalent to diag(H(w), I), H(w) = [psi_(i+j+1)(w)] the (h/2) x (h/2) moment matrix of psi(w) = (Omega(w) + k + 1)/(k Omega(w) + (k + 1)^2) mod k^h written in Y = k^2 + k; (3) Gamma^(k) = [k - i - j is a power of two]_(i, j < J) is invertible over GF(2) for every k (det Gamma^(2c) = det Gamma^(c) det Gamma^(c-1), det Gamma^(2c+1) = det(Gamma^(c))^2; equivalently the S-fraction 1/(1 + z/(1 + z/...)) of sum z^(2^r - 1)); (4) with l = u/(1 + u), (1 + l) Z = Z_0 + l S + sum_r a^(2^r) l^(2^r)/(1 + l^(2^r)) M_(k^(h - 2^(r-1))); (5) for the reduction M of that family to ker X_b along a complement containing k G Y^j (2j < k - 1): [l] M_ij = [l^2] M_ij = 0 for i + j <= k - 2 (2i < k - 1) and [l^3] M_ij = [Y^(h - 2 - i - j)] N for 2i, 2j < k - 1; hence every eigenvalue 1/a has exactly k mod 2 Jordan blocks of size 1, none of size 2, and exactly one of size 3 when k is even and none when k is odd, and for k <= 2 these are all ([1], [3]). Computed exactly, the registered target: the symmetric reduction M of Z to ker X_b with the monomial complement has M_ij = u^(2k - 1 - 2(i + j)) ([k - i - j a power of two] + O(u)), its leading part the Hankel matrix of u^-1 Y^k L(u^2/Y), at every a for sides 8 to 64 (before registration), 128 (after) and 256 (the stress run); with (3) this is the chain lemma (G Y^j heads a Jordan chain of exactly 2k - 1 - 4j, these being the blocks). The leading form beyond the anti-diagonals i + j >= k - 2 (orders 4 and up) is not proved.
failure_conditions: A side 2^m and a in GF(2n)* at which the sparse Taylor form fails, or the partial multiplicities of H(w) at a differ from those of Z(w) (computed false at every a for sides 4 to 128 and 8 to 64).
A k at which Gamma^(k) is singular over GF(2) (proved false; computed false for k < 1000).

A side, a and (i, j) at which M_ij has a nonzero coefficient below u^(2k - 1 - 2(i + j)), or its coefficient there differs from [k - i - j a power of two] (computed false at every a for sides 8 to 256; 128 checked after registration, 256 in the stress run).
foundation_claim_scope: The square torus of rule-60 rings with equally spaced law-(12, 12) contacts, cut open by a ring of cuts each way (A30, A32, A37, A38); its walk over GF(2), at sides 2^m. The spectrum is a contact-level reading, so it does not depend on how the rings are declared (A45).
